messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Missing backup approver mechanism",
 "problem_statement": "Claims handlers are unable to process reserve adjustments when the primary approver is unavailable. This lack of delegation causes claims to stall indefinitely in the approval queue.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "we’ve got a couple of claims held up because the approver’s out and there’s no backup — the approval waiting list is piling up.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-28T08:19:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "can we also review the roles assigned to our claims handlers? Some tasks are getting stuck in the queue.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-16T12:52:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "When a reserve change goes beyond what a handler can approve, it just sits there — that reserve authorisation delay has caused real issues for us, especially when the approver’s out and no one’s covering.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-18T12:10:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "we’re seeing claims stuck because reserve changes need approval but no one’s covering for the approver right now.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-21T13:07:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "reserve adjustments above our team’s limit just sit there until the one approver comes back — no backup, no delegation, and claims pile up.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-10-17T16:58:00Z"
  },
  {
   "quote": "when a handler needs to adjust a reserve beyond their limit, it goes into an approval waiting list — but if the approver’s out, nothing moves.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-28T08:08:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "When a handler needs to adjust a reserve beyond their limit, it goes into an approval waiting list — but if the approver’s out, nothing moves until they return.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-10-28T08:08:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "When a reserve exceeds authority and the approver’s out with no delegate, it just piles up — that approval waiting list causes unnecessary delays... it’s claims stalling until someone returns.",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-14T10:43:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "reserve changes are waiting for an approver who’s on leave — no delegate set up. Claims are stalled because reserve changes beyond handler authority are stuck in an approver’s queue with no backup",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-17T13:03:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "the reserve authorisation delay blocks everything until the approver returns.",
   "route": "support",
   "date": "2026-09-21T13:07:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "claims held up because when a reserve change exceeds authority, it sits in one approver’s queue with no delegate, and that creates a backlog on the approval waiting list",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-25T10:50:00+00:00"
  },
  {
   "quote": "No delegate at all — and it’s causing delays on reserve updates that need sign-off before we can process payments.",
   "route": "account_management",
   "date": "2026-09-25T10:50:00+00:00"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "I checked the claim that reserve adjustments stall when the primary approver is unavailable due to a missing backup/delegation mechanism. Multiple quotes across support, sales, and account_management (Sept–Oct 2026) consistently describe claims stuck in the approval waiting list with no delegate, e.g. 'reserve adjustments above our team's limit just sit there until the one approver comes back — no backup, no delegation.' This is a product capability gap (absence of a delegation feature), not a pricing, contract, IT, or staffing issue, and it recurs across customers and routes over multiple weeks.", "verdict": "pass"}
